source: docs/svs2-ablation-2026-10-24.md (§2-§9, pre-registered before any paid batch). svs2_report.py evaluates this file, svs2_plan.py prices its stages, run_ab.py reads the arm structure, the rotation, the seed keys and the run-arms guard from it. The doc is the normative text.

order._note: One cell at a time. Per (task, rep) the three arms run back to back; the first arm is arms[(rep - 1 + seed + i) % 3], i the task's index in unit.tasks, so it rotates from rep to rep and from task to task (run_ab.arm_order with rotation_offset). A, B and C are interleaved in one batch; the baselines never run.

structure._note: Manipulation checks per cell (run_ab.py validity) and per template home (prepare: each arm's dump differs from stock's only in the slice row). stock and slice are the baseline arms of 2026-10-23 (imported, never run; their entries serve the import and the offline stand-ins). a, b, c: 16 tools (the host's 12 plus the four recall tools), short tape header, long tool lines, compaction allowed and recorded. System-prompt markers: a keeps the slice persona; a, b and c carry the edit-guard rule's phrase 'never re-read a file just to be safe' and lack the 'recorded file read' sentence; b and c lack the persona; the baselines lack the new phrase. dump_rows_vs_slice: the rows an arm's dump may differ in from the baseline's archived dump-slice.yml (svs2_checks.py dumps): none for a and b, the slice-agent-loop row for c, whose packaged config turns history.workingSet on; stock's home, built for the comparison only, must equal the archived dump-stock.yml.

unit.pairing: a new cell pairs with the baseline cell of the same task and rep index (pairing.baseline_cells); the arm side of a pair is the mean of the arm's valid cells at that rep index (one from the batch, a second only from the arbitration); c1, c2 and r2 have deterministic content, f1's content is seeded from the baseline cell's seed key with the baseline's salt, so every f1 pair has byte-identical content

pairing._note: Read-only import: svs2_report.py import-baseline recomputes every baseline cell's metrics row from its archived session log with this harness's ab_metrics (one extractor for both sides) and refuses when any previously stored metric differs; validity, pass, verify info and exam classes are the baseline's own.

min_pairs._note: Per arm against STOCK (and the same against SLICE). Planned 15 pairs (c1 4, c2 4, r2 4, f1 3) and 16 memory items (f1 4 x 3, r2 1 x 4); the cost ladder's deepest step keeps c1 3, c2 3, r2 2, f1 2 = 10 pairs and 10 items. Below a minimum the dependent interpretation is 'inconclusive'.

validity.cell_counts_only_if: as gates-svs.json validity (turn exits, log found, fingerprints of the arm's own offline cells, tool count and names, one turn per prompt, no host path in the system prompt, tape forms, isolation, delivery of r2 T2/T4 and f1 T3/T5), plus the arm's system-prompt markers (structure system_contains / system_lacks)
validity.pair_rule: a pair counts when its baseline cell was valid and the arm has at least one valid cell at that rep index
validity.memory_exclusion: as gates-svs.json: flagged access up to the last exam turn, a leak before the exam, or the oracle via the file system, in the baseline cell or in every valid arm cell of the pair, drops the pair from the memory comparison only

comparisons.cost: off-peak sheet (peak is exactly 2x every field, so ratios do not depend on the sheet); billed tokens of every loop request, failed attempt and compaction summarizer call
comparisons.R_t: per arm X and comparison arm Y, per task: sum over the task's valid pairs of the X side (mean cost of X's valid cells at that rep index) / sum of the Y side

primary.N_code: geometric mean of R_c1 and R_c2, arm / STOCK

secondary: N_code3 = geometric mean of R_c1, R_c2, R_r2 (arm / STOCK)
steps: A / SLICE (the edit-guard rule; cross-batch), B / A (the persona; within the batch), C / B (working-set retention; within the batch), C / A
sum ratio and median paired ratio per task
re-read classes per arm and task (first, cross_turn, same_turn, after_own_edit, edits_writes, bash_writes, fs_not_observed, fs_stale_version)
requests per turn, steps per turn, step-cap cuts, cache hit rate, peak and mean request tokens, slice folds, kept-raw tape entries (C)

quality.dS: sum over valid pairs of pass(arm side, the fraction of its valid cells that passed) - pass(STOCK cell); dS_t per task
quality.dM: correct memory items (arm side mean) - correct items (STOCK) over memory-eligible pairs (f1 4 items, r2 1)
quality.dB: bad items (wrong, decoy, stale, hedged, confabulated; arm side mean) - bad items (STOCK)

quality_floor._note: Q holds iff dS >= -1, no task with dS_t <= -2, dM >= -1 and dB <= +1 (arm against STOCK): no arm may lose more than one pass or one memory item to STOCK, nor gain more than one bad answer.

rules.label: inconclusive
rules.if: any minimum not met (or N_code or R_f1 not computable)

rules.label: fixes the short-session overhead but loses the long-session saving
does not fix the short-session overhead

decision.order: per arm, top to bottom; the first rule that matches gives the arm's interpretation

steps._note: A change 'moves the cost' when the step's geometric mean of R_c1 and R_c2 (and, separately, its R_f1) is <= 0.95 (down) or >= 1.05 (up); otherwise 'no measurable effect at this n'. Reported, not a decision: A/SLICE is cross-batch, B/A and C/B are within the batch.

arbitration.trigger: per arm, on the batch, before pooling: the arm's interpretation would change if N_code or R_f1 moved by 0.05 in either direction, or Q is decided at its margin (dS = -1 or -2, some dS_t = -1 or -2, dM = -1 or -2, dB = +1 or +2), or a minimum is not met
arbitration.what: for each triggered arm: one more cell at every rep index of the tasks behind the marginal quantity (N_code: c1 and c2; R_f1: f1; the quality floor: the tasks whose dS_t or memory decides; a minimum: the tasks below it), same seed keys, batch name 'arb', seed 20261025, arms of a group rotated as in the batch
arbitration.priority: if the budget condition does not hold for every triggered (arm, quantity), they are taken in this order while it holds: N_code before R_f1 before the quality floor; arms a, b, c; the rest stay unarbitrated and are marked so
arbitration.budget_condition: ledger spend + the arbitration estimate (svs2_plan.py, measured per-cell means) <= cap - reserve - margin ($8.65)
arbitration.decide_on: the pooled batches (the arm side of a pair averages its valid cells), the same rules and thresholds, minimums unchanged; no band test and no second arbitration

baseline_per_cell_peak._note: mean cost per cell at peak of the baseline's pooled pairs (record of 2026-10-23 §13.3)
baseline_per_cell_peak._hello: an upper bound: the 2026-10-23 warmups cost $0.0038 for 6 cells and $0.0006 for 3

prior.rule: per new cell before any is measured: max(SLICE, STOCK) per task for c1, c2, r2, hello, and SLICE's for f1 (every new arm seals like SLICE), times the safety factor

stages.note: the floor: 2 reps of every task

budget.ladder: stages run in this order, which is the reverse of what is cut first: r2 reps 3-4 (S5) go first, then c1/c2 rep 4 (S4), then f1 rep 3 (S3), then c1/c2 rep 3 (S2); S1 is never cut. Before the batch the full design must project to <= planning_target with the arbitration reserve; before each stage the projection (ledger + this stage at measured per-cell means, priors where nothing is measured yet, + the arbitration reserve) must stay <= cap - reserve - margin, else that stage and every later one are skipped and the record says so

arbitration_reserve._note: kept free for the most likely single arbitration: N_code of one arm (c1 and c2, one more cell at each of 4 rep indices)
